thread:
anya (AE): Quick sync — EuroFin wants a short POC. Key asks: stream responses from Go client over WebSocket, function-calling (structured JSON output), EU-only data residency, short-lived creds (STS style), and a cheaper quantized variant. Any immediate blockers on our side?

samir (SE): We can support that stack. Go SDK has WS streaming and falls back to SSE. Function-calling/structured output is just schema + tool/api model calls.

kevin (Solutions Eng): Quick sample for Go WS + function-call pattern (send, then parse structured tool output):

```go
// pseudo-sample - minimal flow
conn, _ := ws.Dial(ctx, "wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood/quant-4bit-eu", nil)
// send user message with function spec
msg := `{\"type\":\"input\", \"text\":\"Create payment instruction\", \"functions\": [{\"name\":\"create_payment\", \"schema\": {\"type\":\"object\", \"properties\": {\"amount\": {\"type\":\"number\"}}}}]}`
conn.Write(ctx, ws.MessageText, []byte(msg))
// read stream and look for function_call frames
```

kevin (Solutions Eng): For EU residency, point them to region param: set host to eu.api.redwood.ai or set deployment=private-eu in the request. Hosted EU region keeps data plane in eu-west-1.

lucy (SRE): Security checklist: EuroFin requires SOC2, customer-managed KMS integration, and audit logs retention 12 months. Hosted EU satisfies data residency but for KMS integration they need Dedicated or Private (VPC). Also note: short-lived creds we support via our STS token exchange endpoint for Dedicated/Private; hosted API only supports scoped API keys with IP allowlist.

anya (AE): So hosted won't do short-lived STS + customer KMS. Customer prefers hosted for speed but insists on STS. Do we have a hybrid suggestion?

samir (SE): We usually propose two options: 1) Dedicated reserved pool in EU with STS + KMS — meets all security asks (higher cost, predictable throughput), or 2) Hosted EU + gateway sidecar that mints short-lived tokens from their IdP to our API key rotation service — less ideal, adds infra on customer side and is not fully supported for KMS.

kevin (Solutions Eng): Regarding latency/cost: quant-4bit reduces tokens cost ~2-3x but increases p95 slightly. If they need p99 < 200ms for short prompts, recommend Dedicated with GPU profile optimized for latency + small seq-length config. We can run a short perf benchmark in their environment.

anya (AE): Pricing ask: they want ballpark monthly for a 50k monthly active users read workload (avg 40 tokens/req) on quantized model with streaming. Any rough numbers?

samir (SE): Rough calc: tokens/month = 50k * 40 = 2M tokens. Hosted quant tier ~ $0.0015 /k token (example) -> ~$3k/month token cost + request overhead. Dedicated reserve would be a fixed VM/GPU monthly + lower per-token compute. I'll ping pricing to produce an estimate.

lucy (SRE): Also add compliance uplift for Dedicated/Private (support and audit fees). I'll attach standard SOC2 attestation pack once we open the NDA/ticket.

kevin (Solutions Eng): Minor integration note: function-calling over streaming sometimes splits frames; recommend the client buffer by frame_type==\"function_call_end\" before JSON parse. Share our small helper lib in the Go SDK for that.

anya (AE): Great. Next steps: Samir — prepare 2-option proposal (Hosted-EU w/ gateway pattern vs Dedicated-EU with STS+KMS), include perf estimate and rough pricing. Lucy — prepare SOC2 + KMS checklist and any additional SSO/IdP notes. Kevin — drop Go sample snippet and helper link in the ticket.
